Meeting Minutes 1 - Discussion Summary

Author

Edith

Published

May 27, 2026

Meeting Information

Item Details
Date 27 May 2026
Time 15:30 – 18:00
Venue LKSLIB 2-04
Present All

Opening

The meeting was called to order at 15:30 by Haley at LKSLIB. All three members were present. The team reviewed the agenda and approved it.

Discussion on Mini Challenge Selection

Haley opened the discussion by proposing that the team proceed with Mini Challenge 2.

Haley said: “Mini Challenge 2 offers more challenging data processing methodologies. This gives us opportunities for deeper analysis compared to Mini Challenge 1.”

Edith responded positively, noting that the challenge would allow the team to observe more meaningful patterns within the dataset.

Edith said: “The dataset in Mini Challenge 2 has greater potential for advanced visualisations, especially network-based visualisations like node-link diagrams and Sankey charts.”

Helen agreed and added that the cybersecurity and security detection focus of Mini Challenge 2 aligns well with the team’s academic background and interests.

Helen said: “Since our backgrounds are in cybersecurity and systems administration, this challenge is a natural fit for us.”

Conclusion: The team unanimously agreed to proceed with Mini Challenge 2.

Discussion on Shiny Application Features

The team then discussed what features the Shiny application should include. Haley proposed that the application should not just show visualisations but guide users through a complete investigative narrative.

Haley said: “The application should tell a story from start to finish, how the post was generated, what it means, and how to prevent it from happening again.”

The team agreed on six core features:

# Feature Proposed by
1 Sequence Reconstruction (interactive timeline) Haley
2 Message Generation Chain (Sankey diagram) Edith
3 System Context Overview (agent ecosystem map) Helen
4 Content Provenance Analysis (trace tokens to source) Haley
5 Historical Pattern Detection (find past incidents) Edith
6 Intervention Simulation (one high-impact fix) Helen

Discussion on Quality Scoring Mechanism

Haley raised an additional idea during the discussion.

Haley said: “What if we develop a rule-based algorithm to assign quality scores to different event attributes? We could highlight potentially problematic posts directly in the Shiny interface.”

Edith and Helen supported the idea.

Haley said: “That would help users identify suspicious patterns more effectively.”

Conclusion: The team agreed to explore this feature for Question 2.

Discussion on Website Theme

Haley proposed a blue colour theme for the project website.

Haley said: “Blue fits technology and cybersecurity. It will give our application a professional and cohesive brand identity.”

Helen and Edith agreed. No other colours were proposed.

Task Allocation

The team distributed responsibilities as follows:

All members accepted their assignments.

Task Owner
Data processing + Question 1 Helen
Main page (website) + Question 3 Haley
Meeting minutes + Question 2 Edith

Agreement: Members will update one another regularly on progress and discuss integration during future meetings.
